fatal_errors: The proposed SRO manipulation is causally confounded: annealing can alter defects or phase state, while Mn or Fe additions change composition, lattice distortion, and fault energies independently of SRO.
The experiment does not directly quantify SRO or local shear-fault-energy fluctuations, so strength and dislocation-shape changes cannot be uniquely attributed to the proposed mediator.
explanation: The hypothesis addresses the general strength problem in FCC concentrated alloys and is supported by cited atomistic work on hard atomic motifs and local fault-energy fluctuations. It is nevertheless not a reconstruction of the target study, which used temperature-dependent single-crystal CRSS, strain-rate jumps, TEM, and MSAD calculations to identify lattice-distortion strengthening, cryogenic inertial dulling, and high-temperature Cottrell-type solute pinning. The generated proposal is restricted to room temperature and predicts neither the target composition trends nor its cryogenic and Portevin–Le Chatelier regimes. Its evidence also overstates the role of enhanced SRO: E3 indicates that persistent random-alloy strength is dominated by local fault-energy fluctuations, whereas SRO-associated strengthening can decay after repeated slip. Direct SRO characterization, matched thermal histories, and a same-composition intervention would be needed for a discriminating causal test.
